page.layout: One page of text in two columns, with marginal notes in the left and right margins; the upper section is full-width notes and text above a full-width heading block; the lower section has two parallel columns. Page number at top left. Running head at top centre. Right margin carries small numerals (section marks).

main_text.p: hB. Illum intulissent] Nonæ Olympiadis anno altero, secundum Pisan. Mæssen. De hoc bello vide præter citatos à Bong. Lactantium. lib. 1. cap. 20. qui nonnihil variat.

iDucem Palantum] Strabo lib. 6. auctor est, eos cum seruis Helotibus in Spartanorum ciuium necem hoc modo, vt simularent; in foro pilei lacænici tolerentur, impressio fieret in ciues cœgregatos, & vrbs occuparetur. Quo decreto consilio Parthenię (ita enim legendum esse recte Bongarsius monuit, & apud Strabonem dicuntur παρθενίαι) vitam fuga redemerunt.
kTyrtæum] Qui elegiaco carmine id bellum descripsit, vt liquet è Pausania, qui aliquot eius versus narrationi suæ interseruit.
lPeloponnenses] Hæc igitur ἀφορμὴ prima exstitit belli Peloponnesiaci, quod Thucydides 8. libris persequitur, vetustate proximus ab Herodoto, lectuque multis nominibus vtilissimus.
mPericlem] Anaxagoræ philosophi discipulum, qui dicendo fulgurare, tonare, permiscere Græciam ait in oratore Cic ex Aristophane. Alia ipsius encomia vide apud Thucyd. lib. 2. & Plutarchum Periclē.
nEt ad invidiam impetum declinandum] Simile exemplum Livius de Hannibale & Fabio Max. dictatore commemorat lib. 2 decad. 3.
main_text.head: POMPEII TROGI EPITOMA HISTORIARVM. LIBER IV.
BREVIARIVM.
main_text.p: 1 Siciliæ insulæ situs, fontes, ignes Ætnæ montis, Scyllæ, Charybdis mirabile, rerum naturam; item & Charybdis mirabilium. 2 Nomina, incolæ veteres, imperium Siciliæ ambiunt, & pro-
tyrannis Siciliæ, cui Carthaginenses inhiant. 3 Rheginenses ab Himeræ ranis oppressi. Athenienses

page.notes: Page is a scan of a two-column printed page with heavy staining; the lower two-column block was read in parallel and some words at column edges are uncertain. Right margin numerals (1–40) are section marks and are not transcribed as text. Lower lines are partly illegible and may contain errors.
